title: CFPB to regulate buy now, pay later companies like Affirm, Klarna
summary: News clip on the CFPB announcing plans to regulate BNPL companies and the market's reaction.

assertions.quote: the U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau announced plans to begin regulating businesses like a firm

verdicts.note: The CFPB opened an inquiry into major BNPL providers and later issued an interpretive rule applying credit-card-style protections.

CFPB press release notes that in May 2024 it issued an interpretive rule confirming BNPL lenders must provide consumers legal protections that apply to conventional credit cards, following earlier 2022/2023 market-monitoring inquiries.

KC Fed: the CFPB adopted a 2024 interpretive rule requiring BNPL providers to give consumers the same dispute rights and protections as credit card issuers, an act of applying consumer-lending oversight.

This CFPB report is itself the product of market-monitoring orders the agency issued in December 2021 to five major BNPL lenders (Affirm, Afterpay, Klarna, PayPal, Zip) to gather loan data -- a direct instance of US regulators investigating and asserting oversight over major BNPL companies.

assertions.quote: she wasn't approved even though... you would think that her credit wouldn't be an issue

verdicts.note: Anecdotal but consistent with the fact that BNPL lenders do decline some applications based on their own underwriting criteria.
CFPB: 73% of applicants were approved for BNPL credit in 2021 (up from 69% in 2020), meaning more than a quarter of applicants were denied.

assertions.quote: a firm shares are moving down... regulation maybe profits get hit

verdicts.note: Observable in the stock-price reaction of publicly traded BNPL lenders following regulatory announcements.

assertions.quote: you don't want to have a credit crisis triggered where so many people are taking on debt that they're not equipped to pay off

verdicts.note: A reasonable extension of general lending-risk principles, though BNPL's small loan sizes limit the comparison to prior credit crises.
KC Fed: benefits and risks of BNPL are most salient for financially constrained consumers, who may be more likely to miss repayments or overextend themselves.
